meta.title: How long federal civil cases take: outcomes, class actions and pro se share by district, nature of suit and year
meta.attribution: Source: Probative, How long federal civil cases take: outcomes, class actions and pro se share by district, nature of suit and year, version 1.0.0, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23739969, licensed CC BY 4.0.
meta.citation: Probative. (2026). How long federal civil cases take: outcomes, class actions and pro se share by district, nature of suit and year (Version 1.0.0) [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23739969
meta.disclaimer: Not legal advice. These are counts, medians and shares from the Federal Judicial Center's court records, kept for marketing planning. A court's typical time to disposition says nothing about how any one case will go.
meta.notice: Probative is a marketing firm, not a law firm; not legal advice.

records.text: In fiscal years 2023 to 2025, the District of Alaska resolved 926 civil cases in the group "All civil cases"; the median time from filing to disposition was 199 days. 1,093 cases were filed; 0.2% alleged a class action and 48.1% had a pro se plaintiff.
records.unit: days, median from filing to disposition, cases resolved in fiscal years 2023 to 2025
